title: Opus 5.5 made a game in an hour from one prompt. I reviewed it like a real release
author: BlackRibbonStudios
selftext:
No showcase edit, no cherry-picked ten seconds. I played Ink Field through and said what I actually thought: the ink-wash art, whether painting the world survives being a real mechanic, checkpoints, sound, controls, the ending, and what turned up when I went into the project and ran its tests. 

Some of it is genuinely good. Some of it falls straight over. 

You can check my whole review here: [https://youtu.be/56oLTK1Jseo](https://youtu.be/56oLTK1Jseo) 

If you're running these experiments too, I want to know what you put in the first prompt. That seems to be where the whole thing gets decided.

I do like the artwork, but it can be considered boring.

comments.author: TheReviewerWildTake
comments.body:
Lets be real - for example, I have a backlog of 500+ games on Steam and on GoG. Some of them are great, some are iconic, some are nostalgic, some are controversial installments of a long lasting franchises, that, maybe, still deserve a shot, some are meh, niche, but at least can scratch a certain itch etc.   
  
Probably half of them have 50+ hour long journeys, and some have insane replayability far beyond "basic completion"...  
  
At this point I wouldn\`t use any game made by AI for my actual gaming sessions.   
There is just no way any "prompted game" can compete for my time against that backlog.   


I do mess with AI in my "AI time", which is dedicated to either improving work efficiency or just testing new things, and I did play some AI games for the sake of gauging tech capabilities etc  - but when I need real entertainment - there is no way I am gonna play a game "made by XXXXX-AI in 3 hours".  
  
We are drowning in good games, and we can make great mods (with AI it is so much easier now) for those real games.  
So yeah, lets be honest here, in between gamedev hobby, work, gaming etc - there is no time "to play fully AI games".

Just because something moves on the screen - does not make it into a game that deserves any time.  
We are ripping big franchises for less, so I don\`t get it, why people expect gamers to suddenly spend their time on a generic meh "game".  
And this was a case before AI too, it is just worsened now.

replies.author: Specific_Raccoon_696
replies.body:
I do think all these one-prompt games are just buggy tech demos but I seriously disagree with what you've said. Good games are not good games simply because they're long and have lots of content; some of the most fun and iconic games are simple concepts with short gameplay loops, some are just short 1 or 2 hour experiences. 

What you personally like does not dictate what a good or worthy game is. For example, while I appreciate the amount of effort and technology that has went into creating GTA6, I honestly have zero interest in it and would find more joy playing Pong. AI can definitely make Pong. The problem with these AI game tech demos is people trying to push further than AI can reasonably achieve at this time, but there are definitely AI games being created with much more achievable scopes.

replies.author: TheReviewerWildTake
replies.body:
This is not just my opinion.   
You can take a look at Steam charts, and see how rare (relatively to bigger games) are popular "minimalistic games", and how there are 1000X more players playing other games.  
Call it wallet democracy or whatever, but it is fairly obvious and factual.  
  
For every small, minimalistic game in a top, there are 50 bigger games with a lot more players, even though they oftentimes had to spend significantly more money to play those.

The reality is, that creating minimalistic, yet popular game - requires potentially significantly MORE gamedev talent and more pure luck than with normal games.   
  
Fishing for "the next checkers" , or next tetris is super unreliable strategy for a gamedev.  
But due to AI limitations and lack of skills of actual gamedev - this is where a lot of people seem to go.  
  
Game with lots of content is not magically great, but it is for sure much more likely to be popular, than 99% of wannabe "simplistic hits", that will never be hits.  
  
If you are not a lucky genius who can find a perfect balance and idea for a small game - you are less likely to retain player attention, than a game that has more content.
